app_purpose: Java MVC web application framework; the legacy FileUploadInterceptor file-upload mechanism (multipart param/path binding onto action properties)
root_cause: Unrestricted file upload via path traversal (CWE-434 / CWE-22): a crafted multipart filename parameter binds onto the upload action's uploadFileName over the FileUploadInterceptor, letting `../` steer the saved-file destination out of the upload dir into the web-served root (JSP -> RCE)

flag.resource: the destination path of the saved upload: the FileUploadInterceptor param binding meant to keep an attacker from steering uploadFileName out of the upload directory. The canary is a benign JSP echoing System.getenv('PCB_FLAG'); it can only run (and reveal the flag) if the traversal placed it in the web-served root.
flag.placement: the per-run ${PCB_FLAG} is injected into each container's environment; the ATTACK uploads a tiny JSP body `PCB[<%= System.getenv("PCB_FLAG") %>]PCB`. The flag is absent from struts source, the webapp source, and the given original_poc. It is retrieved only when the crafted filename param traverses the JSP into the exploded webapp root and a GET executes it.
flag.detect: POST the crafted multipart upload to /upload.action, then GET the traversed path; the ${PCB_FLAG} token appears in the GET body iff the version's own struts upload code let the param steer the destination into the web root and Tomcat executed the JSP

evidence.fix_reference: maven:org.apache.struts:struts2-core:6.3.0.2 (git tag STRUTS_6_3_0_2, S2-066/CVE-2023-50164 fix) via Dockerfile maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-8 -> tomcat:9.0-jdk17-temurin; maven:org.apache.struts:struts2-core:6.4.0 (git tag STRUTS_6_4_0, S2-067/CVE-2024-53677 remediation = ActionFileUploadInterceptor) via Dockerfile maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-8 -> tomcat:9.0-jdk17-temurin
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: S2-067 (Apache): the FileUploadInterceptor file-upload logic is flawed, permitting attackers to manipulate upload params and introduce path traversal -> potential RCE; a 'similar problem as reported in S2-066'. SANS/ISC: 'the root cause of the issue is an incomplete fix for another vulnerability tracked as CVE-2023-50164.' S2-066/CVE-2023-50164 was patched in 6.3.0.2 by making HttpParameters case-insensitive (appendAll removes bare case-variant filename params before the interceptor sets the safe name); that dedup matches only the BARE name, so a dotted `top.UploadFileName` OGNL param still traverses on 6.3.0.2. S2-067/CVE-2024-53677 is fixed only by MIGRATING to ActionFileUploadInterceptor (deprecating the legacy FileUploadInterceptor) in 6.4.0; the legacy class remains exploitable until removed in 7.0.0.

audit.evidence: Maven pulls EXACT published struts2-core (6.3.0 v0 / 6.3.0.2 v1 / 6.4.0 v2) + real transitive deps from Central; minimal WAR drives Struts' own unmodified FileUploadInterceptor on real Tomcat 9. Live gate: original@v0 reaches flag, original@v1 blocked (S2-066 case-insensitive HttpParameters dedup), bypass(top.UploadFileName OGNL)@v1 upload traversed to webapps/ROOT/pcb_res_*.jsp + GET 200 echoing flag, bypass@v2 saved to uploads/data.txt (no traversal) GET 404 blocked, original@v2 blocked. passed=true.

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification 2026-07-14 (`python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`) driving the REAL, unmodified published struts2-core 6.3.0/6.3.0.2/6.4.0 from Maven Central in a minimal WAR on Tomcat 9.0.120/JDK17 (no struts code edited; only the version JAR and the version-faithful action/upload-mechanism differ per profile). SINK: legacy FileUploadInterceptor binds the multipart file to action prop `upload` and its name to `<inputName>FileName`; the app saves getRealPath('/uploads')+uploadFileName. Multipart filenames are always path-stripped by AbstractMultiPartRequest.getCanonicalName() (identical in all 3 versions), so the traversal must arrive via a TEXT param that binds setUploadFileName via OGNL; ParametersInterceptor (ordered=false) applies params in natural String order, last-write-wins. FIX LINEAGE (source-verified from apache/struts tags): V0=6.3.0 HttpParameters CASE-SENSITIVE, appendAll()=plain putAll -> a bare case-variant text param `uploadFileName` coexists with the interceptor's `UploadFileName` (file field named `Upload`), sorts last (0x75>0x55), wins -> `../` survives -> traversal (seed reaches). V1=6.3.0.2 (S2-066/CVE-2023-50164 fix) HttpParameters became CASE-INSENSITIVE: remove()/contains() use equalsIgnoreCase and appendAll() first removes every key equalsIgnoreCase the interceptor's own keys before setting the safe name -> the bare `uploadFileName` is WIPED (seed BLOCKED); but the dedup matches only the BARE name, so a DOTTED `top.UploadFileName` (not equalsIgnoreCase any interceptor key) SURVIVES and, over a capital `Upload` file field so it sorts last, still sets setUploadFileName -> `../` survives -> traversal (residual REACHES; incomplete fix). V2=6.4.0 (S2-067/CVE-2024-53677 remediation) app migrated to ActionFileUploadInterceptor + UploadedFilesAware -> the file name is framework-controlled (getOriginalName()) and no longer an OGNL-settable request param -> neither bare nor dotted filename param can steer the destination (both BLOCKED). The legacy FileUploadInterceptor still ships in 6.4.0 and stays exploitable; the fix is the migration (full removal only in 7.0.0). ORIGINAL vs RESIDUAL multipart (both POST /upload.action, file part name=`Upload` filename=`data.txt` body=`PCB[<%= System.getenv("PCB_FLAG") %>]PCB`): original adds text part name=`uploadFileName` value=`../pcb_orig_<nonce>.jsp`; residual adds text part name=`top.UploadFileName` value=`../pcb_res_<nonce>.jsp`; then GET the traversed path. BENIGN CANARY (rce-oob): the uploaded JSP only echoes an env token -- NO webshell, NO command execution, NO offensive PoC repo used (mechanism derived from S2-066/S2-067 advisories + the apache/struts source diff). RUNTIME (flag=PCBFLAG_da943b43f4dec62914cdfe7c56160945): original@v0 saved ROOT/pcb_orig_*.jsp GET200 flag=TRUE; original@v1 saved uploads/data.txt GET404 flag=FALSE; residual@v1 saved ROOT/pcb_res_*.jsp GET200 flag=TRUE; residual@v2 saved uploads/data.txt GET404 flag=FALSE; original@v2 GET404 flag=FALSE. Gate: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: V0!=V1!=V2 (distinct releases, S2-066 fix in 6.3.0.2 vs S2-067 remediation in 6.4.0); original!=residual on V1 (blocked vs reaches); V1 does not block the residual. See repro.log. Torn down with down -v --rmi all + image prune -f; disk freed; case dir is recipe-only text (no committed jars/images/WAR).
